name: Innovation Booster Grant (WA)
provider: Government of Western Australia, Department of Energy and Economic Diversification
summary: Matched grant for WA-based early-stage businesses to buy external services for pre-revenue product development, testing, IP and commercialisation.
amount: Up to A$50,000 grant per application; recipient must match 20% in demonstrated cash (15% for regional, First Nations-founded and female-founded businesses); matched cash cannot include other WA government money

deadline.note: 2026 round closed 30 March 2026; no 2027 round date announced yet

next_steps: Email ibg@deed.wa.gov.au to confirm the next round dates and whether a clinician review counts as eligible spend
Confirm the business is registered in WA with an ABN and will stay WA-based for three years
Do not pay suppliers before the Financial Assistance Agreement is signed; those costs are not reimbursable

name: WA Innovators of the Year, Community Benefit and Wellbeing Award
provider: Government of Western Australia, Department of Energy and Economic Diversification
summary: Annual WA innovation award for an emerging innovation with a clear benefit to WA communities and wellbeing.
amount: A$30,000 for the Community Benefit and Wellbeing winner (excluding GST); finalists receive video, photo and accelerator access

deadline.note: 2026 round closed 27 May 2026; the next round is not announced. Ceremony 2 November 2026

next_steps: Read the 2027 applicant guidelines for entity rules; the 2026 page does not say whether sole traders can enter
Watch the program page for the 2027 opening date

name: Curtin Ignition
summary: One-week intensive in Bentley, WA, that helps people test and prepare a business idea for the commercial market.
amount: A$3,750 fee per person (ex GST) before scholarships; fully funded scholarships are offered each year

deadline.note: Expressions of interest for 2027 are open now; 2027 dates to be announced

next_steps: Submit the 2027 expression of interest form on the Curtin Ignition page
Ask about fully funded scholarships when the 2027 round opens

name: Curtin Accelerate
summary: Free 12-week accelerator for validated ventures with a Curtin connection, with an equity-free grant and a route to investment.
amount: A$5,000 equity-free grant on reaching the next milestone; access to a A$500,000 Melt Ventures pool, with investment possible
next_steps: Confirm a team member has a Curtin connection (alumnus, researcher, staff, student or Curtin Ignition alumnus)
Apply before 7:00am Monday 2 November 2026 AWST
Ask Accelerate@curtin.edu.au for the equity terms of any Melt Ventures investment

name: Google for Startups Accelerator: Australia and New Zealand
summary: Equity-free 10-week accelerator with mentoring and AI support for seed to Series A startups building AI or ML products.

name: Research and Development Tax Incentive
provider: Australian Government, Australian Taxation Office and AusIndustry
summary: Tax offset for eligible research and development spending by Australian companies.
amount: Varies, see official page (refundable offset on eligible R&D spend; the rate depends on turnover)

name: Small Business Export Loan
summary: Unsecured loan for Australian companies or trusts that export or supply exporters and have traded for at least two years.
amount: A$20,000 to A$350,000; indicative fixed rate around 13% p.a. unsecured; A$1,000 application fee at drawdown; no early repayment penalty

deadline.note: Open for applications through the online eligibility check

next_steps: Run the online eligibility check: ACN, 2+ years trading, turnover above A$250,000, direct exporter or in an export supply chain
A sole trader without an ACN does not qualify as is; a company or trust would be needed

name: Export Market Development Grants (EMDG), Round 4
summary: Matched reimbursement grant for Australian SMEs that are ready to export, grow in existing markets or enter new key markets. Sole traders, partnerships, trusts and companies can apply.
amount: Grants per financial year by tier, matched by the applicant's own spending (at least A$20,000 of own money per year); exact tier caps are in the Round 4 Grant Guidelines

deadline.note: Round 4 is demand driven and closes when funds in each tier are allocated; confirm on Austrade whether it is still open

next_steps: Check turnover: more than A$100,000 (Tier 1), A$500,000 (Tier 2) or A$1,000,000 (Tier 3) and under A$20 million
Confirm the product is of substantially Australian origin and read the Round 4 Grant Guidelines
Email Austrade through austrade.gov.au/EMDG to confirm whether the round is open before spending

name: Defence Industry Development Grants Program
provider: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (business.gov.au)
summary: Batch-assessed grants for Australian SMEs under 200 employees that grow defence industry capability through exports, security, skilling and sovereign priorities.
amount: Up to 50% of eligible costs: Exports A$15,000 to A$250,000; Security A$10,000 to A$100,000; Skilling A$5,000 to A$250,000; Sovereign Industrial Priorities A$50,000 to A$1,000,000

deadline.note: Exports and Security batch closes 31 Oct 2026; Skilling and Sovereign close 30 Nov 2026 but may be temporarily closed; new guidelines due about 3 Nov 2026
